title: Security: Lightning Web Security, CSP, data exposure, and Apex access
objectives: Explain Lightning Web Security as an org-wide architecture, not a per-component flag or API version.
Separate LWS distortions from Content Security Policy and from Apex CRUD/FLS.
Treat wired and Apex data as immutable and avoid exposing extra fields or secrets in the browser.
Call Apex only through @AuraEnabled methods you intend to expose, preferring cacheable=true for read-only wire access.
diagnostic_question: A third-party script works in a scratch org, fails in production, and an Apex method returns fields the UI never shows. Which of Lightning Web Security, CSP, data exposure, or Apex access do you inspect first?
definition: Lightning Web Security (LWS) is the current Lightning UI security architecture that isolates namespaces and applies JavaScript distortions so components can use third-party code with less XSS risk. It is enabled by default for orgs created in Winter ’23 and later and is generally available for LWC and Aura as of Summer ’23. LWS is org-wide: it cannot be disabled per component and is not tied to an API version. Content Security Policy (CSP) is a neighboring browser policy for which resources may load. Data exposure is what you put in the browser. Apex access is which @AuraEnabled methods a component may import. ([Lightning Web Security](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/security-lwsec-intro.html); [Call Apex Methods](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/apex.html); [Client-Side Caching](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/apex-result-caching.html))
why_it_matters: Candidates collapse LWS, Locker, CSP, and sharing into one word 'secure.' Enabling LWS-only features then discovering another component cannot run under LWS is an org-wide trap. Returning extra fields from Apex is data exposure even if the template hides them. @AuraEnabled is an API surface.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of an airport checkpoint. LWS is the scanner that isolates each airline's bags (namespaces) and distorts dangerous tools. CSP is the posted list of what you may carry on. Data exposure is leaving a boarding pass on a cafe table—the browser already has it. Apex access is the airside door: only badge methods you marked @AuraEnabled get through, and a read-only door can be cacheable. The scanner is for the whole terminal, not one gate.
deeper_explanation: LWS is modeled after TC39 usable-security ideas. Components run in an isolated JavaScript environment per namespace but can import from other namespaces as if they shared an environment. Most Locker-compliant code keeps working. You may refactor to LWS-only features, but that is a one-way org decision. ([Lightning Web Security](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/security-lwsec-intro.html))

LWS cannot be disabled on individual components and is not associated with an API version. If you adopt an LWS-only feature (for example importing a module from another namespace) you cannot roll one component back to Lightning Locker later. Test every custom Lightning component before production enablement. ([Considerations Before Using LWS-Only Features](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/security-lwsec-refactor.html))

LWS applies distortions to JavaScript APIs. LWS Distortion Viewer documents which APIs are blocked or modified. CSP is a separate control that restricts script, style, and remote hosts. Do not treat a CSP block as an LWS distortion or the reverse. ([LWS Distortion Viewer](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/security-lwsec-tools-distortion-viewer.html))

Call Apex by importing @AuraEnabled methods and wiring or invoking them. Treat provisioned data as immutable; copy before mutate. Prefer the least data: UI API wires honor CRUD, FLS, and sharing, while Apex returns whatever the method queries unless you enforce user mode/FLS in Apex (APEX-014). cacheable=true is required for @wire to Apex and is only legal on methods that do not mutate data. ([Call Apex Methods](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/apex.html); [Client-Side Caching](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/apex-result-caching.html))

mental_model.analogy: An airport checkpoint: scanner (LWS), carry-on list (CSP), boarding pass left on a table (data exposure), airside badge door (Apex access).
useful_mapping: whole-terminal scanner → LWS is org-wide, not per component
distortion → a tool that is allowed but changed so it cannot cut the fence
CSP poster → which scripts and hosts may load
boarding pass on the table → fields in JS memory / extra Apex columns
badge door → @AuraEnabled import surface; cacheable=true is a read-only door
where_it_breaks: A real airport can close one gate; you cannot disable LWS for one component.
CSP is not a scanner distortion; it is a different control plane.
A closed door does not replace sharing: Apex can still over-query if the method is careless.

teach_back_prompt: Explain LWS versus CSP versus Apex access to a teammate using the airport checkpoint, then name one place the analogy breaks.

claims.claim: LWS is enabled by default for orgs created in Winter ’23 and later, and LWS for LWC and Aura is generally available as of Summer ’23.
LWS cannot be disabled per component and is not associated with an API version. LWS-only features prevent a later Locker rollback for that component.
LWS distortions block or modify JavaScript APIs; look them up in LWS Distortion Viewer. CSP is a sibling security topic, not the same control.
claims.validation: Distortion Viewer topic and security nav that lists CSP separately.

claims.claim: LWC calls Apex by importing exposed methods; treat returned data as immutable. cacheable=true is required for @wire and only allowed on non-mutating methods.
claims.validation: Call Apex Methods and Client-Side Caching.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: LWS is org-wide namespace isolation plus JS distortions, not a per-component flag. CSP is which resources load. Data exposure is extra fields in the browser. Apex access is the @AuraEnabled door, with cacheable=true only for reads you wire.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I never say 'Locker is dead in every org' without checking. I will not adopt an LWS-only import until every component is tested, because I cannot disable LWS for one bundle. I prefer UI API wires when they suffice because they honor CRUD, FLS, and sharing. If I write Apex, I return the minimum fields and treat the payload as immutable. Hiding a field in the template is not security.

terminology.plain: The current Lightning UI security architecture that sandboxes JavaScript by namespace.
terminology.precise: Default for orgs created Winter ’23+. GA for LWC and Aura as of Summer ’23. Org-wide, not per component, not an API version. Distorts or blocks some JS APIs.
terminology.example: A third-party chart library that needs a listed distortion reviewed in Distortion Viewer.
terminology.non_example: A profile permission that hides a tab.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lightning Locker: the previous default architecture.
terminology.boundary: Sharing and CRUD are not LWS.

terminology.plain: The older Lightning component security architecture LWS replaces as the default.
terminology.precise: Some Locker restrictions are unnecessary under LWS. Adopting LWS-only features means you cannot put that component back on Locker.
terminology.example: An org created before Winter ’23 that still has Locker until an admin enables LWS.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent a Locker API version.

terminology.plain: Browser rules for which scripts, styles, and hosts a page may load.
terminology.precise: A sibling of LWS in the Lightning security documentation set. A blocked CDN is often CSP, not an LWS distortion.
terminology.example: A remote font host refused by CSP.
terminology.boundary: Exact header strings Need verification per org type.

terminology.plain: Putting fields, IDs, or secrets in the browser that the UI does not need.
terminology.precise: Anything Apex or a wire returns can be read in DevTools. CSS hide and lwc:if are not authorization. Prefer UI API adapters that honor FLS, or Apex that returns a narrow DTO.
terminology.example: Apex returning SSN while the card shows only Name.
terminology.non_example: A user without FLS not receiving a field from getRecord.

terminology.plain: Which Apex methods an LWC is allowed to import and call.
terminology.precise: Methods must be exposed (@AuraEnabled). Import and @wire or call imperatively. cacheable=true required for wire and forbidden for DML. Treat results as immutable.
terminology.non_example: SOQL written in the LWC JavaScript file.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: LDS ui*Api wires that do not use your Apex.
terminology.boundary: Governor numbers are APEX-007; do not invent them.

terminology.plain: A change LWS makes to a JavaScript API so unsafe behavior cannot run as-is.
terminology.precise: Viewer lists blocked or modified APIs. If an API is not listed, native behavior is allowed. Third-party libraries may need updates.
terminology.example: Looking up document.cookie behavior in Distortion Viewer after a library fails.
terminology.non_example: A 413 from too many batched Apex actions.
terminology.boundary: Look up the current API; do not memorize an unofficial list.

when_to_use: When a security review asks how Lightning Web Security, CSP, data exposure, and Apex access differ for an LWC.
When a third-party library fails and you must choose Distortion Viewer versus a CSP host block.
When Apex returns fields the UI never shows and you need to reduce data exposure.
When deciding whether an @AuraEnabled method may be cacheable=true and wired, or must stay imperative.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this security lesson as a substitute for org-wide sharing design, MFA, or Apex user-mode details (SEC and APEX-014).
Do not treat LWS as a per-component flag or an API version, or disable it to paper over a CSP or library problem.
Do not hide extra Apex fields in the template and call that data exposure solved.
Do not mark a DML method cacheable=true so you can @wire it.

decisions.rejected: lwc:if to hide revenue and keep returning it

decisions.because: Named-credential secrets do not belong in the browser.
decisions.rejected: Store the token in a private JS field

decisions.decision: Check Distortion Viewer and CSP separately for the chart library; do not disable LWS for one component.
decisions.because: LWS is org-wide and not per bundle.
decisions.rejected: Request Locker just for the chart

No token properties on the DTO.

decision_table.signal: A remote script or font is refused by the browser as an untrusted host.
decision_table.choose: Inspect Content Security Policy and trusted URLs.
decision_table.not: Disable Lightning Web Security for the whole org to 'let the script through.'
decision_table.why: CSP is a sibling control plane; LWS is not a per-host allow list.

decision_table.signal: A JavaScript API behaves differently than on a raw HTML page.
decision_table.choose: Look up the API in LWS Distortion Viewer and adapt the library.
decision_table.not: Assume CSP blocked it, or request a per-component LWS off switch.
decision_table.why: LWS distorts or blocks APIs org-wide; there is no per-component disable.

decision_table.signal: Apex returns unused confidential fields the template does not render.
decision_table.choose: Stop querying them; shrink the DTO or switch to an LDS wire for those fields.
decision_table.not: Hide the fields with CSS or lwc:if and call the page secure.
decision_table.why: Data exposure is what reached the browser, not what the user sees.

decision_table.signal: LWC needs read-only Case fields via Apex and @wire.
decision_table.not: cacheable=true on a method that updates records so the wire compiles.
decision_table.why: The caching guide allows cacheable only when the method does not mutate data, and wire requires it.

limitations: Does not replace sharing, profiles, or MFA.
Does not enumerate every LWS distortion or CSP header.
Does not teach user-mode Apex in full (APEX-014).
Does not authorize toggling LWS in production.
security_notes: Never return secrets, session IDs, or named-credential tokens to LWC.
LWS-only features are an org-wide commitment.
Apex limits apply per invocation; do not invent a number beyond the documented 2,500-action batch / 413 note.
common_mistakes: Adopting LWS-only imports before testing the org.
Hiding extra Apex fields in the UI.
Treating CSP and LWS as the same switch.

troubleshooting.symptom: Third-party library works locally in a plain HTML page, fails in Lightning.
check: LWS Distortion Viewer for the APIs it uses.
CSP for the hosts it loads.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: You can disable LWS for that one component.

troubleshooting.symptom: @wire to Apex will not compile or run.
check: Does the method DML? Then it cannot be cacheable.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The import path is the only issue.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users can see a field in DevTools they cannot see on the layout.

production_notes: Test LWS in a full-copy or partial sandbox with every custom Lightning component before production enablement.
No production LWS toggle is authorized by this lesson.

interview_questions.question: Separate Lightning Web Security, CSP, data exposure, and Apex access.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: LWS sandboxes JS org-wide. CSP limits loaded resources. Data exposure is extra payload in the browser. Apex access is the @AuraEnabled door.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I refuse a single word 'secure.' LWS distortions are API behavior. CSP is hosts and scripts. If SSN is in the XHR, that is exposure even when hidden. If the method is not @AuraEnabled, LWC cannot import it. cacheable=true is a read-only cache contract, not a security fairy.
interview_questions.example: Chart CDN blocked by CSP; eval distorted by LWS; extra Apex column in DevTools.

interview_questions.question: Why is LWS a one-way org decision once you use LWS-only features?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: LWS is org-wide and not per component. An LWS-only import cannot run under Locker, so you cannot flip one bundle back.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I test every custom Lightning component before production LWS enablement. I delay cross-namespace LWS-only imports until that gate passes. Interviewers listen for 'not an API version' and 'not js-meta.xml.'
interview_questions.example: One unlocked-package widget imports another namespace; a legacy Aura chart then fails under LWS.
follow_ups: Does Aura also run under LWS?
weak_answer_warnings: We will disable LWS on the broken component

interview_questions.question: Apex returns unused confidential fields. How do you fix data exposure?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Stop returning them. Shrink the DTO or use an LDS wire. Hiding in the template is not a fix.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the network payload, not the screenshot. I prefer getRecord when FLS should strip fields. If Apex stays, I select only UI fields and add a review that new properties need a reason. I never stash a token 'for later' on the DTO.
interview_questions.example: labCaseBadge dropped AnnualRevenue and a named-credential token from the wrapper.

interview_questions.question: You want to @wire an Apex updater that closes a Case. What is wrong?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Wire requires cacheable=true, and cacheable methods cannot mutate data. Close the Case imperatively instead.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I split reads and writes. The closer is an imperative method without cacheable. After it succeeds I refreshApex on the read wire or notify LDS. I do not mark DML cacheable to silence the compiler.
tradeoffs: Two methods versus one god method
follow_ups: What if the read is LDS not Apex?

interview_questions.question: A library works in a gist and fails in the org. Walk LWS versus CSP.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If a host or script is refused, CSP. If a JS API misbehaves, Distortion Viewer. Do not disable LWS for one component.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I reproduce with debug mode. I check the console for CSP. I look up APIs in Distortion Viewer. I read third-party library LWS notes. I may fork or replace the library. I will not recommend a production LWS off switch from this lesson.
interview_questions.example: Chart fetch to an unlisted CDN versus document.cookie distortion.
tradeoffs: Replace library versus adapt to distortions
follow_ups: Who owns CSP in the org?

interview_questions.question: Users without FLS still see a field in your LWC. What do you inspect?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Whether Apex returned it. UI API wires omit inaccessible fields; careless Apex does not.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I compare getRecord versus the Apex JSON. I check the method's sharing and FLS handling—that detail is APEX-014, but the LWC lesson is: do not over-query. I treat this as data exposure plus an authorization bug, not an SLDS issue.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Apex wrapper selected a hidden custom field the layout never showed.

interview_questions.question: When would you not write Apex for an LWC data need, for security reasons?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When a record form or UI API wire already returns the least data and honors CRUD, FLS, and sharing.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The Call Apex Methods topic starts with 'make sure there isn’t an easier way.' Security is part of that easier way. I write Apex when I need a join, an action, or logic LDS cannot express—and then I still return a narrow DTO. I do not write Apex to bypass FLS.
interview_questions.example: Name and Phone on LAB_ Contact via lightning-record-view-form, not a custom SOQL class.
follow_ups: What if I need a related aggregate?

interview_questions.question: Teach LWS, CSP, exposure, and Apex access with an airport checkpoint, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Scanner is LWS for the whole terminal. Poster is CSP. Boarding pass on the table is extra fields. Badge door is @AuraEnabled. You cannot close the scanner for one gate.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The break: a real airport can shut one gate; LWS cannot be disabled per component. Another break: a locked door does not stop a careless method from handing over extra bags—Apex can over-query. I never call this a library catalog.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard four boxes plus 'org-wide' stamped on LWS.
